surfaces.part: umbrellas (contents sticking out of the opening)

answer.evidence: The container body has a single bright rim line at row 22 (L=244), and the front face runs below it in rows 23-30 with a dark base at row 31. The width profile is a constant 14 from row 18 to row 30. It never widens and narrows again, so there is no ellipse mouth. The opening is not seen from above, and the opening itself is hidden behind the umbrellas. The dark navy columns at the sides in rows 18-21 are the back wall outline, not a top surface. The umbrellas (rows 3-21) are contents and decor, and no inside floor or surface is visible between the rim and the umbrellas. This matches the 'rim only' red examples, so the container reads as a front elevation with a 1-row rim.
